sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
TypeScript = **structural type system** on top of JS.

- **Compile-time only** — types are erased, no runtime cost.
- **Inference** is the killer feature — annotate at boundaries, infer inside.
- **Generics** — `<T>` for reusable abstractions.
- **Utility types** — `Partial`, `Pick`, `Omit`, `Record`, `ReturnType`.
- **`unknown` > `any`** — narrow before use.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:

- **Types and interfaces** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Structural vs nominal** — TS is structural; you can't enforce branded identity without `& { __brand }`.
- **Discriminated unions** — the senior pattern for state machines.
- **`strict` mode** — non-negotiable; turn it on day one.
- **Type narrowing** — `typeof`, `in`, custom predicates (`x is T`).
- **`any` is a smell** — it leaks, and the type system stops helping.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd model the domain with discriminated unions, narrow with custom type guards, expose minimal generic surfaces, and run with `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. `any` is a debt I track in code review."*
